properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 6 at 2:15PM EST by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
At 214 PM EST, Doppler radar was tracking strong thunderstorms
capable of producing a landspout along a line extending from near
Farmville to Willard. Movement was east at 20 mph.

HAZARD...Landspouts and wind gusts up to 40 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Minor damage to outdoor objects is possible. Gusty winds
could knock down tree limbs and blow around unsecured
objects.

Locations impacted include...
Greenville, Jacksonville, Kinston, Winterville, Ayden, Farmville,
Wallace, La Grange, Grifton, Phillips Crossroads, Kornegay, Stokes,
Rose Hill, Snow Hill, Richlands, Bell Arthur, Beulaville, Deep Run,
Catherine Lake, and House.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with these storms and may lead
to localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

These storms may intensify, so be certain to monitor local radio
stations and available television stations for additional information
and possible warnings from the National Weather Service.

properties.description:

was located 9 miles northwest of Mount Olive, moving east at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree damage is
likely.

This dangerous storm will be near...
Mount Olive and Mount Olive around 215 PM EST.

Other locations impacted by this tornadic thunderstorm include
Grantham, Brogden, and Mar-Mac.
properties.instruction:

floor of a sturdy building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors, in a
mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter
and protect yourself from flying debris.

properties.instruction:

current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Saipan
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 6 at 3:18PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
A developing tropical disturbance, Invest 99W, is quickly approaching
the islands of the northern CNMI. The Joint Typhoon Warning Center
(JTWC) has issued a Tropical Cyclone Formation Alert (TCFA) for 99W.
This means that development into a significant tropical cyclone is
likely within the next 24 hours. What this means for the northern
CNMI of Alamagan, Pagan and Agrihan is that you can expect an
increase in showers and thunderstorms with strong gusty winds as 99W
moves past. Invest 99W is currently not expected to move through the
northern CNMI stronger than a Tropical Depression. However, as with
all tropical cyclones, this could change.

Invest 99W is currently moving fairly quickly, which is a good thing
for the northern CNMI. At the current speed, 99W looks to pass
through the region near Alamagan Saturday morning or early afternoon,
not becoming a Tropical Storm until later in the day, west of the
islands. Invest 99W will be monitored over the next 24 hours for any
significant changes in expectations and the residents of the
northern CNMI should continue to monitor forecasts for any changes to
the current expectations. For now, prepare for increasing rainfall,
with isolated thunderstorms and strong gusty winds within the heavier
showers. Only 1 to 2 inches of rainfall is expected, with gusts up
to 40 mph possible.

For more information on Invest 99W, see bulletins issued by JTWC
under WMO header ABPW10 PGTW and WTPN21 PGTW.

NWSheadline: INVEST 99W APPROACHING THE ISLANDS OF ALAMAGAN, PAGAN AND AGRIHAN
